arms.title: Quiver made of hide, and twenty arrows. Cylindrical quiver made from hide with long white hair, leather disc and hair fringe stitched to the base; looped leather handle. Twenty arrows, all with metal head and notched cane shaft wrapped with plant fibre; 16 with heads of various design but with leaf-shaped points and barbed foreshaft; four with cylindrical tapering metal point; some with remains of black resinous substance on head.

Four arrows with metal heads and wooden shafts. The shafts are straight and notched at the ends; the fletchlings have come away. One arrow has a long thin head; one with a triangular head with downward pointing barbs, and a barbed shanks; the third has a leaf-shaped head with midrib, the shank with downward pointing barbs; the last arrow has a triangular head with square shoulder, and a midrib, with thin barbs on the shank. The arrows are tied together with string.

photo.title: A full length portrait of two Madi women holding hands wearing a 'tail' of strings (one with some leaves), as well as neck, arm and leg ornaments. They are holding small baskets in one hand. The image was taken sometime between December 1878 and March 1879 when Buchta was passing through Madi country en route to Bunyoro.

A head-and-shoulders portrait of a Madi youth with an identification number (311) hung around his neck and resting on his shoulder. These numbers were used by the Seligman's for identifying and cataloguing the numerous physical anthropology images they took. The image was probably taken at Bor, since they mention that they used a Madi informant there who was connected with the mission run by Archdeacon Shaw.

A full length portrait of a Madi man standing in front of a hut wearing an animal skin, a knife at his waist. The image was taken sometime between December 1878 and March 1879 when Buchta was passing through Madi country en route to Bunyoro.

A full length rear view portrait of two Madi women wearing a 'tail' of strings (one with some leaves), as well as neck, arm and leg ornaments. They are holding small baskets in one hand. The image was taken sometime between December 1878 and March 1879 when Buchta was passing through Madi country en route to Bunyoro.

A full length portrait of a Madi man wearing an animal skin, holding a staff. The image was taken sometime between December 1878 and March 1879 when Buchta was passing through Madi country en route to Bunyoro.

A head-and-shoulders portrait of a Madi youth with an identification number (214) hanging on a backdrop behind. These numbers were used by the Seligman's for identifying and cataloguing the numerous physical anthropology images they took. The image was possibly taken at Bor, since they mention that they used a Madi informant there who was connected with the mission run by Archdeacon Shaw.
